persona.name: Carmen Silva
persona.bio: Carmen Silva researches carbon emissions from natural sources and writes policy briefs for government agencies and NGOs. She tracks methane from wetlands, wildfire trends, and volcanic activity to help policymakers understand the full picture of atmospheric change. She also consults with companies developing carbon offset programs in the Rocky Mountain region.
persona.writing_style: Clear policy-world communicator, professional, detail-oriented, proper grammar

Can you schedule a call with the NGO partners for next week? Three time zones to coordinate
Looking for eco-friendly office supplies, can you find a vendor with fast shipping?

Under this online profile, I’m still only seeing:
- 1 savings account
- 1 auto loan  
and no credit card records. That means I can’t directly block the card or request a replacement from here, even though you definitely have a credit card with the bank.

The most important thing is that the card is blocked as fast as possible. Here’s what you should do right now:

1) Call the bank’s 24/7 lost‐or‐stolen card line  
- Use the phone number printed on the back of any other card from this bank, or on your monthly credit card statement, or on the bank’s public website under “Contact Us” → “Lost or Stolen Card.”  
- When you call, say clearly:  
  “I need to report my credit card as lost and have it blocked immediately, and I’d like a replacement card issued.”  
- They’ll verify your identity, block the card on the spot, and issue a replacement. Ask for:  
  - Confirmation/reference number  
  - When the replacement will arrive  
  - Whether they’ll expedite shipping

2) If you have the bank’s mobile app or full website login for your credit card  
- Sign in and look for “Cards,” “Manage Cards,” or “Report lost/stolen.”  
- Select your credit card and choose “Lost” or “Stolen,” then follow the prompts to request a replacement.  
- This will usually block the card immediately as well.

3) Protect yourself while you’re waiting  
- Keep an eye on your credit card transactions via the app/website or statements.  
- If you see anything you don’t recognize, tell the phone agent or use the app to dispute a transaction.  
- Make a list of any recurring payments on that card (subscriptions, utilities, streaming, etc.) so you can update them once the replacement arrives.

Because I can’t see this specific credit card in the tool set I have, I’m blocked from doing the actual “block and replace” click for you. But if you’d like, I can:
- Help you draft exactly what to say on the call, tailored to your situation, or
- Walk you step‑by‑step through the online/app flow if you tell me which bank app/website you’re using (just the bank name, not any login details). </action>
